newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pictet rates Surveillance a hold.
newsitem.headline: Pictet rates Surveillance a hold.

text.p: Swiss private bank Pictet & Cie said it had removed Societe Generale de Surveillance Holding SA (SGS) from its list of non-rated stocks and now rate it a "hold."
Pictet said in its latest weekly note that SGS's bearer shares were currently trading at 18.8 times prospective 1998 earnings and the registered share at a price/earnings ratio (p/e) of 17.2.

But given the possibilities for a share buy-back programme, Pictet said it believed the effective multiples for the stocks are probably nearer to 16.6 times for the bearer and 15.5 times for the registered share.
In view of the prospects of a steadily rising earnings curve and based on the valuation of the stock, Pictet said it rated the stock as a "hold."
SGS's share price has come under pressure from the Swiss tax authorities' decision to apeal against a tax panel's ruling that upheld SGS position in a dispute over share buy-backs.

In addition, Pictet said there had also been some pressure on SGS' stock as a result of an expected shortfall in both fee income and profits stemming form the non-renewal of government inspection contracts.
On June 4 SGS said it expected the 1997 group net profit to decline from 1996's 262.7 million Swiss francs, due to a loss of earnings from the termination of several contacts.
